Title: Open Redirect via X-Forwarded-Prefix Header in redirectTrailingSlash
Analysis:
The `redirectTrailingSlash` function in `gin.go` extracts the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header and passes it to `path.Clean()`. However, it does not validate that the resulting prefix is a relative path or does not point to an external domain. Specifically, a malicious client can supply a URL or a path starting with double slashes (e.g., `//example.com`) or a directory traversal structure in the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header. 

When a request matches a route that triggers `redirectTrailingSlash` (e.g., requesting a path that requires a trailing slash redirection), the header value is used to construct the redirection destination URL:
`p = prefix + "/" + req.URL.Path`
If `prefix` is set to `/../../example.com`, this evaluates to `//example.com/path/`. The browser parses the resulting `Location` header `//example.com/path/` as a protocol-relative URL, redirecting the user to `example.com` (an external domain) instead of the local server, which leads to an Open Redirect vulnerability.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
```http
GET /path2 HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-app.com
X-Forwarded-Prefix: /../../attacker.com

```
This request will return:
```http
HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
Location: //attacker.com/path2/
```
